title: Workday Named as a Market Shaper in the 2026 Gartner® Emerging Market Quadrant for AI Agents in Human Resources — Established Vendors
summary: Workday, Inc. (NASDAQ: WDAY), the agentic platform for HR, finance, and IT, today announced it was named as a Market Shaper in the inaugural Gartner Emerging Market Quadrant (eMQ) for AI Agents in...
body_markdown:
PLEASANTON, Calif.


, Oct. 8, 2026


/[PRNewswire](http://www.prnewswire.com/) / --[Workday, Inc.](https://www.workday.com/en-us/homepage.html) (NASDAQ: WDAY), the agentic platform for HR, finance, and IT, today announced it was named as a Market Shaper in the inaugural[Gartner Emerging Market Quadrant (eMQ) for AI Agents in Human Resources](https://forms.workday.com/en-us/reports/gartner-emerging-market-quadrant-ai-agents-hr/form.html) .


With Workday agents, organizations can speed up frontline hiring, cut case volumes, and resolve payroll issues in minutes instead of weeks, freeing HR teams to focus on strategic work, giving managers more time back to lead their teams, and lifting productivity across the workforce.


Workday agents are designed to anticipate what needs attention, advise on the best next step, and act to get work done, all within the policies, permissions, and business processes organizations already rely on. In HR, that means support across the full employee lifecycle, helping move candidates through hiring, answering employee questions, and finding missing payroll information before it creates a problem. These agents work together behind the scenes so employees and HR teams always have one simple place to ask for help. The results are fewer routine questions landing in HR's support queue, more time for managers to spend managing their people instead of paperwork, and a measurable productivity lift across the entire workforce.


"In HR, the margin for error is effectively zero," said Max Wessel, senior vice president of product at Workday. "That's why Workday agents are built to anticipate what needs attention, recommend the right action, and act — across hiring, payroll, and talent — within the customer's policies and approvals HR teams already rely on."


**Automation Inside the Guardrails Organizations Already Trust**


Workday's agents are lawful by design. They inherit the same policies, permissions, and approval chains already governing recruiting, payroll, and talent processes, so they can anticipate what needs attention, recommend the right action, and act within those guardrails, with a human always in the loop. This is Workday's broader vision for agentic HR: connecting every stage of the employee lifecycle, from hiring to development to retirement, into a single AI-powered system built for trust, transparency, and scale. By automating routine and repetitive work, Workday agents give HR teams back the time to focus on strategic priorities, like talent strategy and workforce planning, rather than case management.


**Delivering Measurable Customer Outcomes**


These results show that agentic HR isn't only about speed — it's about giving HR teams the accuracy and trust to act with confidence. With Workday agents for HR, customers have been able to:


- Automate 95% of frontline hiring, cutting time-to-hire by 70%, giving store managers significant time back each year to use towards operations.
- Surface relevant internal hiring leads to recruiters, resulting in a 15% increase in internal hires.
- Resolve complex payroll questions in under a minute — work that used to take far longer.
